source: Wang et al. (2024) Uncertainty of Thoughts (Table 1 recomputed)
finding: The paper says UoT improves success 'by 38.1%' and 'Success Rate increases 46.6% for Llama3-70B' without saying relative or absolute. I recomputed Llama3-70B from Table 1 (5 datasets, open-set and closed-set, 10 DP/UoT cell pairs). The mean of per-cell RELATIVE gains is 46.6%, the exact paper figure. The mean absolute gain is about 10.1 points. So the headline numbers are relative gains averaged over cells.
numbers: Llama3-70B: mean relative gain 46.61% (paper: 46.6%); mean absolute gain 10.13 points; ratio-of-means gain only 28.8%. Mistral-Large per-cell relative gain 47.0% (open set) and 45.7% (closed set), absolute 8.9 and 9.9 points.
limits: Inference by recomputation, not a statement in the paper. The 38.1, 33.8, 29.9, 28.3, 12.4 figures are very likely the same type (relative, averaged per cell) but only 46.6 was checked. Low base rates inflate relative gains (15.0 to 25.0 is +67%).
agent_relevance: Never compare UoT's 38.1% with BED-LLM's +37.4 percentage points. In absolute terms UoT is roughly +10 points per cell across 20Q, diagnosis and troubleshooting.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Uncertainty of Thoughts, Table 2 and Appendix I.1
finding: At matched token cost (GPT-4, closed set), the information-gain tree beats self-consistency over questions by a wide margin. CoT-SC took 33 samples per turn and picked the most repeated question. Tree-of-Thought with deeper search also trailed UoT at the same cost.
limits: SC here votes on which QUESTION to ask, not on a final answer. All closed-set with GPT-4 as answerer and a given hypothesis set. The Table 2 columns appear averaged differently from Table 1 and the paper does not say how. Single paper; no seeds shown in this table. Token counts are the authors' own.
agent_relevance: Partly closes gap 5: a matched-budget comparison exists for question choice on closed sets. Self-consistency on the final answer at equal tokens is still untested.

source: Choudhury/Bickford Smith et al. (2026) BED-LLM, Table 1 (ICLR 2026), recomputed means
finding: Across 18 cells (3 target sets x 6 LLMs, 100 targets each) full EIG (BED-LLM) beats every ablation in every cell. Replacing EIG by marginal predictive entropy keeps most of the Split gain but loses about 13 points. Implicit maximization (LLM judges the most informative of the same candidates) gives only 8 points over prompting.
numbers: Mean success % over 18 cells (my recomputation from the printed table): Prompt-Only 30.3, CoT 39.5, Implicit Max 38.6, Data-Estimation 42.2, Split 55.4, Entropy 57.6, BED-LLM 70.7, ICL Beliefs (EIG with raw in-context beliefs) 26.8. BED-LLM beats Entropy in 18 of 18 cells; per-cell gap 8 to 23 points (Celebrities, Mistral-Large: 91 vs 68).
limits: Unweighted averages over cells typed from the PDF table; SEM per cell about 4 to 5 points. 20 Questions on famous entities, animals and things only. Prompt-Only baseline is the authors' own.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: with noisy (non-deterministic) answers the entropy proxy is clearly worse than full EIG, and full EIG costs no extra calls over entropy. Use full EIG, not the proxy.

source: Choudhury/Bickford Smith et al. (2026) BED-LLM, Appendix F.1 Fig. 10 and H.3
finding: The EIG estimate converges fast in the number of sampled hypotheses and the ranking of candidate questions stabilises earlier than the values. At 10 hypotheses the order of five candidates already matched the order at 85.
numbers: One game, turn 5, GPT-4o-mini, one target, 5 candidate questions, hypothesis set size up to 85. Defaults in all experiments: at least N=15 hypotheses (up to 3 sample-then-filter cycles), M=15 candidate questions. Fewer than 15 valid hypotheses can remain late in a game.
limits: A single illustrative game, not a systematic study; no token or call counts per N. Stability of the argmax across targets, models and late turns (after filtering shrinks the set) is not measured.
agent_relevance: Gap 2 for 20Q-type probes: about 10 to 15 hypotheses suffice for the choice. Cost scales as N hypotheses + M questions + N x M answer evaluations. A token curve is not given.

source: Choudhury/Bickford Smith et al. (2026) BED-LLM, Sec 3.3, 6.2, A.2.1
finding: Predictive entropy equals EIG only if answers are deterministic given the hypothesis. When answers are noisy, a question can have high answer entropy and zero information (ice cream vs film taste). In preference elicitation (abstract text-profile target, 200 profiles, turns 0 to 5) Entropy gave no improvement over Prompt-Only; Prompt-Only was a stronger baseline there than in 20 Questions; BED-LLM's boost was clearest when questioner and answerer were different model classes.
numbers: 200 ground-truth profiles; 10 film recommendations rated 1 to 5 by an LLM judge each turn. Per-turn scores are only in Fig. 3 (not extracted).
limits: Soft target judged by an LLM answerer and LLM judge, so the signal is noisy. Size of the soft-target advantage unknown to me. The different-model-class finding hints that part of the 20Q gain may come from questioner-answerer agreement.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: EIG advantage shrinks on soft targets but is not shown to vanish. No runtime softness test is in the paper (my inference: call a task soft when the hypothesis space cannot be listed or the compatibility check on sampled hypotheses returns graded or inconsistent answers).

source: Choudhury/Bickford Smith et al. (2026) BED-LLM, Sec 3.1, A, Fig 5-7, Table 1 and 3
finding: Raw in-context beliefs break first, not the EIG maths. Independent sampling of 200 hypotheses shows mode collapse onto a few famous names. Models often sample hypotheses that contradict the history. Filtering removes a large share of samples. Running EIG on unfiltered in-context beliefs scores below plain prompting.
numbers: Table 1 mean over 18 cells: ICL Beliefs (full EIG, no filtering) 26.8 vs Prompt-Only 30.3 vs BED-LLM 70.7. Data-Estimation (LLM proposes hypotheses with probabilities) 42.2. Wall time Qwen2.5-72B, Animals set: Prompt-Only 26 to 45 min, BED-LLM 2h30m, Data-Estimation 1d17h.
limits: Order of failure is inferred from ablations, not from a controlled long-context study. Contexts are at most 20 turns. Sampling, answer model and history are not isolated one by one.
agent_relevance: Gap 8: a hypothesis-consistency filter (does each hypothesis agree with every observed answer?) is the key guard. Without it, adding EIG is worse than not adding it.

source: Kobalczyk, Astorga, Liu, van der Schaar (2025) Active Task Disambiguation with LLMs (ICLR 2025), Sec 4.1 and App F
finding: Explicit EIG over sampled solutions beats implicit and implicit-ToT question choice in 20 Questions (15 animals, 5 seeds, 10 rounds, GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o-mini). The gap is much smaller for GPT-4o-mini. N=20 sampled animals was a good proxy for EIG measured on a 500-animal list. Weighting by model log-probs underperforms uniform weighting.
numbers: Diversity (mean mutual-information score over 330 questions), diverse prompt vs vanilla: N=10 0.57 vs 0.46; N=20 0.58 vs 0.54; N=30 0.60 vs 0.58. Defaults N=20 solutions, M=5 candidate questions. Calls per turn: implicit O(1), implicit-ToT O(M), EIG O(N+M+N*M); code generation O(N+M) because answers come from running code.
limits: Small task set (15 animals). Score is a rank of the target in an LLM-ordered list, not a success rate. No tokens-matched comparison with self-consistency. The authors name the stopping rule as an open limitation.
agent_relevance: Gap 2: diversity of sampled hypotheses matters at least as much as their count; 10 to 20 is the working range. Ask for diverse, representative hypotheses.

source: Kobalczyk et al. (2025) Active Task Disambiguation with LLMs, Sec 4.2 and Tables 3-4
finding: On code (HumanEval, APPS), clarifying test-case questions chosen by EIG (M=5 candidates, answers from executing sampled programs) beat zero-shot questions. Answers come from running code, so evaluation noise is near zero. Gains are larger for weak models and for open (input to output) questions.
numbers: HumanEval accuracy after 4 questions, base(B)/EIG(B)/base(O)/EIG(O): GPT-3.5 70.8/85.6/75.9/85.0; GPT-4o-mini 79.6/81.5/83.5/83.8; Llama3-70B 78.8/87.5/81.2/85.5; Llama3-8B 53.0/65.8/64.8/75.5. APPS GPT-4o-mini 62.9/75.3/75.1/87.2. 48 tasks (APPS 47), 3 run seeds, 3 eval seeds; standard errors about 1.4 to 5.
limits: Baseline is a single zero-shot question, so EIG uses about N+M more calls; no equal-token baseline. Only 4 questions. For the strongest case (GPT-4o-mini, HumanEval, binary) the gain is only 1.9 points.
agent_relevance: Gaps 1 and 3: a code-probe version works and execution removes the answer-noise problem. Strong models gain less, the same pattern as GPT-5 in Battleship.

source: Grand, Pepe, Tenenbaum, Andreas (2026) Shoot First, Ask Questions Later? (ICLR 2026), Sec 2, 4.3, App B
finding: The paper models a noisy answerer as a binary symmetric channel and gives closed-form EIG = Hb(eps+(1-2eps)p) - Hb(eps). More candidate questions sampled (1 to 10) raises the EIG of the best question, up to 0.227 bits (94.2% of the noise ceiling). The Bayes question step alone changes game score only slightly.
numbers: eps=0.1, max EIG 0.531 bits; human mean EIG 0.351, median 0.411. Redundant (EIG=0) questions: Llama-4-Scout 18.5% to 0.2%, GPT-4o 14.6% to 1.2%. Question step alone: F1 +0.021 to +0.026 for Scout and GPT-4o. 54 games per strategy (18 boards x 3 seeds). Full Bayes-QMD: Scout F1 0.367 to 0.764. GPT-5 'does not significantly benefit' from Bayes question or move selection.
limits: Constant noise rate. With constant eps, EIG is monotone in |p-0.5|, so ranking by predictive entropy gives the same order (my derivation). The proxy fails only when noise differs by question. High EIG did not give better play for weak models. Spotter fixed to GPT-5. The 0.67 win rate over GPT-5 includes move and decision modules.
agent_relevance: Gaps 2 and 3: best-of-M question scoring keeps paying up to about M=10 and approaches the ceiling. Strong reasoning models gain little from added EIG selection.

source: Pan, Xie, Wilson (2025) LLMs Think Too Fast To Explore Effectively, Appendix C.1 and C.3
finding: A richer prompt for GPT-4o (CoT, self-reflection, an explicit strategy hint that wider element variety unlocks new possibilities, and a check of past attempts) did not significantly raise discoveries. No prompt gave a computed option-count or empowerment number per candidate.
numbers: GPT-4o with engineered prompt at temperature 1: average inventory 43 elements, t = -1.17, p = 0.304 (GPT-4o baseline 35; humans 42). Feature steering on LLaMA3.1-70B also gave no significant gain. Ablating the SAE empowerment neuron cut empowerment-guided behaviour; ablating the uncertainty neuron caused catastrophic failure.
limits: One model for the prompt test and few runs. The hint was verbal advice, not a computed count the model could copy. So an explicit computed option-count hint has NOT been tested.
agent_relevance: Gap 4 stays open. A scaffold that computes option counts in code and shows them per candidate is a different intervention from the one tested.

source: Song, Gore, Kleiman-Weiner (2025/26) Estimating the Empowerment of Language Model Agents, Table 5 and Sec 5
finding: In the current version, empowerment beats five simple trajectory statistics at tracking discounted reward across model-domain pairs. The correlations are modest in WebArena.
numbers: Spearman with discounted reward, WebArena (N=16 model-domain pairs): empowerment 0.39, visitation entropy 0.16, action entropy 0.09, state coverage -0.04, trajectory length -0.12, unique-state ratio -0.38. tau-bench (N=6 points): empowerment 0.71, visitation entropy -0.71, action entropy -0.54, trajectory length -0.54, state coverage -0.20, unique-state ratio 0.60. Per-domain WebArena values are higher (0.83 to 0.94 in three domains, flat in Shopping).
limits: Correlation across models and domains (aggregate), not prediction of failure of a single run. N=16 and N=6 are tiny; the paper calls the tau-bench pooled value descriptive. Needs a trained encoder and many trajectories per setting.
agent_relevance: Gap 6 partly answered: beats simple statistics on two benchmarks, but only as an aggregate capability score. No per-trace failure-detection result (AUC) exists. Too heavy and too weakly validated as a cheap runtime monitor.

source: Song, Gore, Kleiman-Weiner (2025/26) Estimating the Empowerment of Language Model Agents, tau-bench and authentication sections
finding: On tau-bench airline (50 tasks, 28 to 34% pass) empowerment rises with model size and matches reward rank. On retail (115 tasks, 3 to 7% pass) it inverts, because small models hallucinate diverse invalid tool calls that give varied errors and so high action-state information.
numbers: Airline empowerment: Qwen2.5 1.5B 0.59, 7B 0.71, 32B 0.74. Retail pass rates 3 to 7%. WebArena Shopping flat. Authentication case study: GPT-4o with one-step memory logged in on 137 of 182 runs (75.27%); GPT-4o-mini and no-memory GPT-4o logged in 0 times.
limits: Three Qwen sizes only. The failure (varied errors read as control) is the noisy tool-output case that predictive entropy also mishandles.
agent_relevance: Gaps 3 and 6: tool-output noise breaks information-based scores in the same way. A monitor must check that variety comes from valid, task-relevant outcomes.

source: Lidayan, Du, Kosoy, Rufova, Abbeel, Gopnik (2025) Intrinsically-Motivated Humans and Agents in Open-World Exploration, Sec 2.1 and 2.4
finding: The goal-statement correlation is narrower than the headline. Of 51 children recruited, 26 aged 8 or more were analysed; 17 children and 23 adults gave transcripts; the r=0.8 correlation uses only the 10 children (and 12 adults) with at least 5 utterances. No correlation for adults or for question utterances. Goals were labelled by gpt-3.5-turbo.
numbers: rho = 0.8, p = 0.005 unadjusted, N = 10 children, goal-utterance fraction vs Mean Achievement Score. Children 21% goal utterances vs adults 10%; questions 12 to 13% in both. Word rate vs score correlations in children mostly not significant at 0.05.
limits: Correlational, one environment (Crafter), 20-minute sessions, several tests with no correction, LLM-labelled utterances, subset chosen by speech volume. No replication found. The paper says the small sample limits conclusions.
agent_relevance: Gap 7: not replicated, and the base is 10 children, not 17. Treat 'state your goal' as a cheap hypothesis for the agent, not a finding.

source: Du, Watkins, Wang, Colas, Darrell, Abbeel, Gupta, Andreas (2023) Guiding Pretraining in RL with LLMs (ELLM)
finding: An LLM that proposes goals as intrinsic rewards raises exploration in Crafter, but conditioning the policy on the stated goal did not give a significant extra advantage during pretraining.
numbers: ELLM unlocks about 6 achievements per episode vs 9 for the ground-truth-reward oracle, and beats novelty-only methods (APT, RND, Novelty). 64.9% of suggested goals were context-sensitive and achievable; 5% were disallowed. Goal-conditioned vs unconditioned: no significant difference.
limits: Trained RL agents, not a prompting scaffold. Goals come from an LLM given text captions, not self-stated by the agent. Different mechanism from human private speech.
agent_relevance: Gap 7: no direct test of a goal-stating step in an LLM reasoning scaffold found. The nearest result is neutral for policy conditioning, positive for goal-based reward.

source: Cooper, Wadhawan, Giorgi, Tan, Liang (2025) The Curious Language Model (CuriosiTree), Sec 3.3 and 4
finding: The only LLM paper found here with an explicit stopping rule. Score each action by expected information gain relative to cost, and stop when the top class probability passes a threshold, or abstain when the cost budget is spent. It beats random choice and LLM self-evaluation of which action to take in a simulated diagnosis.
numbers: Utility trades information gain against cost with lambda=0.1; 5 candidates per action class, 20 actions scored per turn; action costs 1 (reasoning), 1 (retrieval), 2 (ask patient), 3 (lab test). 50 trials per method, Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, main text reports only the lupus diagnosis. Success and coverage values are in Fig. 4 (not extracted).
limits: One diagnosis in the main text, 50 trials, arbitrary cost values, LLM-as-judge grading. Threshold and lambda were not swept in the text I read. Preprint.
agent_relevance: Gap 10: a workable rule is stop when max probability passes tau, or when best EIG minus lambda x cost drops below zero. Break-even tuning is not validated.

source: Laban, Hayashi, Zhou, Neville (2025) LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation
finding: Across 15 LLMs and six generation tasks, performance falls in multi-turn, underspecified conversations. Models guess assumptions early, answer too soon, and lean on their own earlier wrong attempts. Most of the drop is unreliability, not lost aptitude.
numbers: Average drop 39% (abstract; Fig 1 caption says -35%): aptitude -15%, unreliability +112%. 200,000+ simulated conversations. SNOWBALL (repeat all prior info each turn) recovers 15 to 20% of the drop; temperature 0 did not remove the unreliability.
limits: Simulated user, sharded instruction tasks, not probe selection. The 39 vs 35 figure differs between abstract and caption. Evidence for history-ignoring in general, not for EIG scoring.
agent_relevance: Gap 8: ignoring or over-trusting history is a main long-context failure. Re-state the live hypothesis set and all observations at each probe step.

source: Golovin and Krause (2011/2017) Adaptive Submodularity: Theory and Applications in Active Learning and Stochastic Optimization
finding: Theory for the greedy policy. If the gain function is adaptive monotone submodular, greedy selection gets at least (1-1/e) of the best adaptive policy for a fixed budget of k probes, and an (ln Q + 1) cost ratio for reaching a coverage target. Noise-free results are the base case; persistent noise is handled only by extensions.
numbers: Fixed-budget bound (1-1/e), about 63%. Cover bound ln(Q)+1 times optimal cost for integer-valued objectives. Generalised binary search gets a (ln n + 1)-type guarantee for noise-free hypothesis identification.
limits: I read the statements, not the proofs. Raw entropy reduction is not claimed to be adaptive submodular in general. Persistent noise (the same probe repeated gives the same wrong answer) is a separate, harder case.
agent_relevance: Gap 10: supports a cost-weighted greedy stopping rule (stop when best gain per cost falls under a threshold) in the noiseless case. For tool outputs with persistent noise there is no clean guarantee.
